source.title: Reference Feature Atlases for Mechanistic Auditing of Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a linear attachment of held-out models to a shared reference-feature coordinate system and cosine comparisons of model support profiles. These are different measurements from representational-distance convergence.
record.gate_note: The study measures target reconstruction from atlas codes and cosine similarity between decoder-support profiles. These bear on linear mapping and a proxy for cross-model alignment, but are not direct comparisons of distances between the same inputs. The refusal steering, hidden-objective interventions, and political-framing interventions do not measure convergence and are omitted.
record.test_reason: This is an auditing-method paper that cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as motivation. Its attachment experiment fits a linear decoder from a panel-trained sparse atlas code to a held-out model's residual stream and reports the loss (Table 2). That is a direct measurement of how well one set of models' representations linearly maps onto another lineage's, so it bears on V4. The support-profile cosines (Fig. 5) compare decoder-norm profiles, not representations, and fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right but incomplete. The authors conclude that a reference atlas gives reusable shared coordinates, and that a linear attachment fit doubles as a panel-relative cross-lineage signature. Their headline results are two: the residual channel recovers and suppresses three LoRA-planted hidden objectives in both held-out targets, beating per-target SAE and crosscoder baselines on Mistral; and it surfaces a panel-relative Qwen political-framing cluster that shifts under intervention. They stress that the Qwen findings are panel-relative, not model-intrinsic.
record.recipe_differences: Uses atlas attachment quality and cosine similarity of decoder-support profiles rather than directly comparing representational distances between the same inputs or measuring convergence with scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Attachment and support-profile results depend on the chosen reference panel: Qwen's held-out attachment to Atlas B differs substantially from its in-panel result in Atlas A.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity of per-coordinate decoder-norm support profiles between attached targets and panel models: in-panel 0.83–0.84, held-out Mistral 0.71, held-out Qwen 0.34. Qwen is also a lower outlier within Atlas A (0.66–0.79 vs 0.74–0.89).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models from different lineages differ in which shared sparse dictionary features they load on, with some lineages (Qwen) notably distant from a Western-trained panel.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-steering directions from atlas coordinates, decoded through a held-out target's attached decoder, raise refusal on held-out targets (Mistral 0.28→0.58, Qwen 0.74→0.98) with 0/100 benign refusals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features learned on one set of models transfer as causal handles to a held-out model via a linear decoder.

record.problems: The study uses two held-out targets from a five-model pool, all models are of comparable 7–9B scale, and it does not test scale or capability trends. The cross-model cosine is over decoder-support profiles rather than direct representational distances. The Qwen political audit is explicitly uncontrolled and panel-relative.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the numerous intervention and hidden-objective outcomes because they do not measure cross-model convergence or mapping quality.

untested.parts: All models are 7–9B. There is no scale or capability sweep.
No same-architecture, different-seed model comparisons. The seeds vary only the atlas training.
Only linear decoding from a sparse multi-model code is tested. Stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, and direct pairwise linear maps between two models are not tested.
No test of whether independently learned features recur across models. Shared atlas coordinates are imposed by construction.
Only one layer (60% depth) and one site are used. Similarity measures and input distributions are not varied.
No measurement of plateauing, and no attribution of alignment to shared data or objectives.

missing.what: In-panel reconstruction of Mistral in Atlas B (KL 0.17, ΔCE +0.08, FVU 0.35), the natural comparator for held-out Mistral rows r1–r3
missing.locator: Table 2, Atlas B Mistral panel row

missing.what: LoRA-merged Mistral attachment reported at FVU 0.117 on held-out neutral text (ridge λ=1000, 52,622 token pairs), apparently inconsistent with FVU 0.59 in Table 2

Panel-model reconstruction FVU ranges (0.31–0.53) and KL (0.17–0.44), showing that the sparse atlas itself loses substantial variance even in-panel, so part of the held-out loss is a bottleneck effect

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily an interpretability and auditing tool paper. Convergence is invoked only as motivation (citing Huh et al.). Only the attachment-quality numbers bear on V4, and they come through a sparse TopK bottleneck rather than a direct model-to-model map. Because of that bottleneck, in-panel reconstruction is the right baseline for judging held-out loss. Five models of similar scale are used, with two held-out targets, a single layer, and three atlas seeds.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of increasing alignment with scale.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations for shared features or subspaces.
Tests linear target-decoder attachment to atlas codes only; does not test stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired activation data.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No systematic variation of similarity measure settings or input distributions to test metric or data dependence.
Cosine similarity is measured on decoder-support profiles, not directly on representation geometry. The study does not test plateauing or whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment.

relationships.condition: Mistral held out, linear attachment to Atlas A (Llama, Qwen, Gemma-2, OLMo-2 panel), 60% depth residual
relationships.reason: A linear map recovers next-token behaviour moderately (KL 0.43, ΔCE +0.27, FVU 0.59; r1–r3). Loss is clearly above Mistral's in-panel reconstruction (KL 0.17, FVU 0.35; from Table 2 text), so the mapping is not 'little loss'.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out Mistral attachment yielded KL 0.43, cross-entropy increase 0.27, and unexplained variance 0.59, versus in-panel KL 0.17 and unexplained variance 0.35.

relation.reason: Held-out attachment directly measures reconstruction and downstream behavioral losses after mapping shared atlas representations into a target model, bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: The attachment experiment uses a different method—linear decoding from frozen shared sparse atlas codes—to test representational interchangeability. The pack identifies a methodological change rather than a distinct new setting.

source_check.notes: Original activations are valid references for KL and ΔCE; in-panel reconstructions provide additional comparators across different atlas panels. Appendix E's Mistral FVU 0.117 concerns fresh LoRA-target attachment and does not replace Table 2's result.
